title: Remaining Python work transferred to approved language owners
summary: Governor directive: all remaining Python work transfers to its already-approved language owner. Go>network search(xingcheng search engine),web/external data acquisition(network I/O),batch files and streaming. Rust>vector indexing,RAG mechanical retrieval(PostgreSQL retains formal data validation),untrusted-data parsing(designated native-security component). Julia>statistics/scientific computation(on-demand analysis),optimization and simulation. FSharp>business rules(non-sovereign domain logic),data validation and transformation. CSharp>business process(application/workflow). Existing C/C++>system scheduling and state(no second Rust/Go scheduler). C++/C>formal model inference(no second inference engine). Python+JAX>model training retained. Python>necessary governance semantics retained. Invariants:Julia does not replace JAX;Rust does not replace the existing C runtime;Go does not replace CSharp workflow;each capability has exactly one formal execution owner.
